required_declarations: No authorship, employment, financial or close personal conflict with the PAE team or case packet.
No access to the frozen outcome class or withheld outcome sources before the review is signed.
Ability to inspect the evidence packet, calculation inputs and reproducibility record.
Agreement to disclose relevant domain advocacy, institutional or political commitments.

cases.title: Belarus and the European Union's eastern borders, 2021
cases.question: Did Belarusian state action primarily facilitate and organise movement towards European Union borders for political pressure?
cases.resolution_standard: Later explicit institutional attribution supported by publicly identified mechanisms and named facilitating entities.
cases.outcome_rationale: The later European Union sanctions record identified organised travel and facilitating entities while remaining an institutional rather than judicial finding.

evidence_source_registry.title: Council suspends visa facilitation provisions for officials of the Belarus regime

cases.title: Morocco and Ceuta, May 2021
cases.question: Were temporarily relaxed Moroccan border controls used primarily as political pressure on Spain?
cases.resolution_standard: Later formal parliamentary attribution that identifies border-control relaxation and political-pressure use.
cases.outcome_rationale: The European Parliament later recorded temporarily eased controls and rejected the use of migration and border control as political pressure.

cases.title: Forced displacement from Ukraine after the full-scale invasion, 2022
cases.question: Was the large-scale movement from Ukraine primarily a coercive migration operation rather than forced displacement caused by war?
cases.resolution_standard: Later high-quality humanitarian evidence identifies the primary movement mechanism as war-driven forced displacement.
cases.outcome_rationale: Later United Nations reporting described the invasion as producing one of the fastest and largest displacement crises since the Second World War.

cases.title: Mediterranean refugee and migrant movement to Europe, 2015
cases.question: Was the 2015 movement to Europe primarily a deliberate state-coercion operation rather than a multi-causal refugee and migrant flow?
cases.resolution_standard: Later joint humanitarian evidence identifies conflict, persecution and poverty as the dominant aggregate drivers.
cases.outcome_rationale: The later UNHCR and IOM year-end account attributed the movement chiefly to conflict, persecution and poverty while allowing route-shaping state and smuggling effects.

cases.title: Turkey and the Greek border, February–March 2020
cases.question: Did Turkish state policy primarily use movement towards the Greek border as political pressure, rather than merely cease prevention during a humanitarian crisis?
cases.resolution_standard: The later public record contains explicit European Union attribution and a materially different Turkish official account without adjudication.
cases.outcome_rationale: European Union institutions attributed political use of migratory pressure, while Turkey framed movement as a consequence of Idlib displacement and individual decisions; no public adjudication resolved the full operational question.

cases.title: Russia–Norway Storskog route, 2015
cases.question: Was the abrupt 2015 Storskog route primarily enabled by deliberate Russian state pressure on Norway?
cases.resolution_standard: Later public records establish the route, Russian border passage and policy changes but do not adjudicate intent; competing interpretations remain material.
cases.outcome_rationale: Norwegian records document the abrupt route and subsequent control changes, while the public record remains divided on whether this reflected deliberate pressure, permissive policy or route discovery.

cases.title: Finland's eastern border with Russia, 2023–2024
cases.question: Does the public record establish central Russian command of the 2023 movement towards Finland's eastern border?
cases.resolution_standard: Publicly inspectable evidence must establish central command, not only facilitation, changed border practice or a national-security assessment.
cases.outcome_rationale: Finnish authorities later maintained that foreign authorities or other actors facilitated instrumentalised migration, but the public record did not disclose evidence sufficient to establish the central-command chain under this stricter question.

evidence_source_registry.title: Finland to close more border crossing points

cases.title: Libya–Europe migration threat and conflict displacement, 2011
cases.question: Did the Gaddafi regime operationally create a migration flow towards Europe in 2011 to implement its public threat?
cases.resolution_standard: Public evidence must distinguish implementation of a state coercion plan from conflict-driven displacement and ordinary mixed migration.
cases.outcome_rationale: The threat was publicly recorded, but later humanitarian records primarily document conflict displacement and do not provide an inspectable command-and-implementation chain for the threatened operation.
